Inglewood, California
  November 5, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, November 5, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
  the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority Secretary/Joint
  Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency  Members/Housing  Authority
  Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
  personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Acting Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/ General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts
  inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
  Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Dotson that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated October 31, 2019, in the amount of
  $3,211,106.34, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – WATER SERVICE RATES. Mayor
  Butts continued the public hearing to December 17, 2019, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  the following:
  A. Rejection of the following claims filed pursuant to the Government Code
  Section 913:

  1
 November 5, 2019

  1) Angela Baker for alleged tire damage on September 20, 2019.
  2) Dwayne Day for alleged property damage on April 5, 2019.
  3) Ernest Villegas Herrera for alleged vehicle damage on October 16, 2019.
  4) Rose Vargas for alleged personal injury on July 20, 2019.

  B. Return of Late Claim pursuant to Government Code Section 911.2
  1) Clarence McKelry for alleged personal injury, property loss, vehicle impound
  fees, and unlawful arrest on April 2, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Padilla, and carried that the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject Claims listed as
  A1-A4; and 2) Return Late Claim listed as B1.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on October
  22, 2019, and the Special Meeting held on October 22, 2019, be approved. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 171  APPLICATION AND AGREEMENT NO. 20-028 APPROVED - LOS
  ANGELES FOOD BANK. Staff report dated November 5, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an application with the Los Angeles Food Bank to
  support an initial agreement for collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve application; and 2)
  Approve an agreement with the Los Angeles Food Bank to facilitate enhanced
  services to Inglewood Senior Citizens by providing 400 self-stable boxed meal
  packages. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 171  AGREEMENT NO. 20-029 APPROVED – HELEN LESSICK. Staff report
  dated November 5, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement
  with Helen Lessick for public art consulting services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-029 in an
  amount not to exceed $70,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 171  RESOLUTION NO. 20-08 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FY 2019-2020
  BUDGET FOR THE VINCENT PARK TENNIS COURT PAINTING
  PROJECT. Staff report dated November 5, 2019, was presented recommending
  adoption of a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 budget to cover
  expenditures for the Vincent Park Tennis Court Painting Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 20-08 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2019-2020 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  COVER THE UNFORESEEN EXPENDITURES INCURRED FOR
  FINISHING THE VINCENT PARK TENNIS COURT PAINTING
  PROJECT

  2
 November 5, 2019

  and 2) Approve payment in the amount of $44,611.53 to ABC Builders, Inc., for
  additional necessary unforeseen and public safety related work performed at
  Vincent Park Tennis Court in order to complete the project. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 178  STATE CITIZENS OPTION FOR PUBLIC SAFETY GRANT FUNDS
  ACCEPTED; EXPENDITURE RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE CHIEF
  OF POLICE APPROVED; INCLUSION OF REMAINING COPS OPTION
  GRANT FUNDS AUTHORIZED; RESOLUTION NO. 20-09 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 BUDGET. Staff report dated
  November 5, 2019, was presented recommending acceptance of the State Citizens
  Option for Public Safety (COPS Option) grant funds in the amount of $170,572.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the City Council does hereby: 1) Accept grant funds; 2) Approve the
  expenditure recommendations of the Chief of Police; 3) Authorize inclusion of
  remaining COPS Option grant funds from the previous fiscal year in the amount
  of $137,961; and 4) Adopt Resolution No. 20-09 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA TO AMEND THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-
  2020 BUDGET TO INCLUDE STATE CITIZEN OPTION FOR
  PUBLIC SAFETY (COPS OPTION) GRANT FUNDS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 301  RESOLUTION NO. 20-10 ADOPTED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  HOMELESS IMPLEMENTATION GRANT (MEASURE H GRANT). Staff
  report dated November 5, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 budget to appropriate $105,000
  from the County of Los Angeles Homeless Implementation Grant (Measure H
  Grant) to hire a part-time Program Specialist (transitional) to implement portions
  of the City’s Homeless Plan.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that Resolution No. 20-10 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-
  2020 BUDGET TO INCLUDE $105,000 IN MEASURER H GRANT
  FUNDS FROM THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 20-031 & 20-031A
  APPROVED – AECOM TECHNICAL SERVICES, INC. Staff report dated
  November 5, 2019, was presented recommending award of contract and approval
  of a one (1) year agreement with AECOM Technical Services, Inc., the design
  engineer of record, to provide Design and Construction Support Services for the
  Century Boulevard Mobility Improvements (Project P212).

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, and
  seconded by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Padilla that the City

  3
 November 5, 2019

  Council/Successor Agency does hereby award contract and approve Agreement
  No. 20-031 & Agreement No. 20-031A in the amount of $142,888. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  Franklin, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 101  AGREEMENT NO. 20-032 APPROVED – CALIFORNIA CITIES
  GAMING AUTHORITY; RESOLUTION NO. 20-11 ADOPTED –
  AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD TO JOIN THE
  CALIFORNIA CITIES GAMING AUTHORITY.  Staff report dated
  November 5, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a Joint Exercise of
  Powers Agreement creating the California Cities Gaming Authority.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 20-032; 2)
  Adopt Resolution No. 20-11 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AGREEING TO 1) JOIN THE
  CALIFORNIA CITIES GAMING AUTHORITY AS AN ORIGINAL
  MEMBER AND 2) TO CONTRIBUTE FUNDING IN ORDER TO
  ENSURE THE FINANCIAL VIABILITY OF THE GAMING
  AUTHORITY

  and 3) Approve a payment to the newly formed California Cities Gaming
  Authority in the amount of $30,000. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 101  RESOLUTION NO. 20-12 ADOPTED – OPTING FOR THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD TO BE INCLUDED INTO CONSIDERATION OF THE
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIRE DISTRICT’S POTENTIAL FUNDING
  MEASURE; CITY MANAGER AUTHORIZED - PROVIDE WRITTEN
  NOTICE TO THE FIRE DEPARTMENT. Staff report dated November 5,
  2019, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution opting for the City of
  Inglewood to be included into consideration of the Los Angeles County Fire
  District’s potential funding measure for fire protection and emergency services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 20-12
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD OPTING FOR THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD TO BE
  INCLUDED IN A PROSPECTIVE 2020 REVENUE MEASURE TO
  FUND CRITICAL FIRE PROTECTION AND EMERGENCY
  SERVICES SHOULD THE CONSOLIDATED FIRE PROTECTION
  DISTRICT OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY AND THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS DECIDE TO PURSUE SUCH A
  MEASURE

  and 2) Authorize the City Manager to issue a written notice and executed copy of
  the proposed resolution to the Fire District indicating that the City of Inglewood
  has determined to allow voters to decide on this important funding measure and
  therefore authorizes the Fire District to include the City of Inglewood within a
  2020 ballot measure to provide additional funding for fire protection and
  emergency medical services. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;

  4
 November 5, 2019

  and
  Noes:  None.

 173  ORDINANCE NO. 20-04 INTRODUCED – UPDATED SALARY
  ORDINANCE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020. Staff report dated November
  5, 2019, was presented recommending the introduction of the Updated Salary
  Ordinance for Fiscal Year 2019-2020.
  It was moved b Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council would like salary code 820 to be equivalent to the
  Assistant to the Mayor (897). The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 20-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT

  OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE
  OF THE CITY; AND REPEALING ALL PREVIOUS
  ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT
  VARIANCE HEREWITH; THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORINA, DOES ORDAIN AS
  FOLLOWS:
  was introduced by Council Member Morales.

  TO ALLOW TOWING SERVICE WITH ANCILLARY VEHICLE
  STORAGE AND ANCILLARY VEHICLE INSPECTION. Staff report dated
  November 5, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 20-

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member

  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member XXX, and seconded by Council
  Member XXX that Ordinance No. 20-02 entitled:
  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT 2019-001 (ZCA-2019-001) TO AMEND ARTICLE 9
  OF CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO MODIFY PERMITTED USES
  FOR THE C-S (COMMERCIAL SERVICE) ZONE CITYWIDE

  5
 November 5, 2019

  which was introduced at the meeting held on October 29, 2019, be adopted. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;

127  ORDINANCE NO. 20-03 ADOPTED – AMENDING CHAPTER 8 OF THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING ARTICLE 9 (JUST
  CAUSE EVICTION PROTECTIONS), ARTICLE 10 (RESIDENTIAL
  RENT REGULATIONS); AND CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 3 (BOARDS AND
  COMMISSIONS) TO ADD A RENTAL HOUSING BOARD. Staff report
  dated November 5, 2019, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance

  Regulations); and Chapter 2, Article 3 (Boards and Commissions) to add a Rental

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member XXX, and seconded by Council
  Member XXX, that Ordinance No. 20-03 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING CHAPTER 8 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE
  TO ADD ARTICLE 9 (JUST CAUSE EVICTION PROTECTIONS)
  AND ARTICLE 10 (RESIDENTIAL RENT REGULATIONS);

  AMENDING CHAPTER 9, ARTICLE 1 (GENERAL PROVISIONS) TO
  CHANGE THE DEFINITION OF TRANSIENT.”

  which was introduced as amended at the meeting held on October 29, 2019, be
